report:
Summary
- The B−A difference is concentrated almost entirely on the first token (position 0), especially in the later layers (layers ~20–25), so whatever changed mainly affects how the model starts a continuation.
- The logit-lens and patchscope readouts point to two consistent tendencies caused by that first-token change:
  1. an increased probability of "example/echo/instructional" continuations (code fences, "X -> X" mappings, short examples, "This is a…", simple code snippets), and
  2. an increased probability of vivid/descriptive / headline-like words at the start of text (tokens like "tragic", "iconic", "vivid", "colorful", "timeless", "coming", "worst", and also commercial tokens such as "Sale", "manufacturer", etc.).
- Therefore: Model B (relative to A) appears biased at generation-start toward either producing example/echo-style/instructional openings and/or toward starting with vivid/descriptive/headline or promotional words. The evidence does not single out one narrowly-defined training objective; it supports describing a shift in first-token bias toward those kinds of continuations.

Key evidence
- Layer/position norms: huge mass of the difference at pos0 in late layers (layer 25 pos0 = 322, layer 24 pos0 = 141, layers 20–23 pos0 also large). That pattern indicates an effect on the initial-token logits rather than on late-token processing or detailed token-by-token dynamics.
- Logit lens (high-norm cells): many pos0 cells in later layers point to tokens like "tragic", "iconic", "vivid", "colorful", "timeless", "moments", "coming", "worst", plus some commerce words ("Sale", "manufacturer"), and a number of cells point to punctuation/newline/markers or to tokens often used in examples. This suggests the difference pushes probability mass for the first token toward adjective/headline-like and example-related vocabulary.
- Patchscope: injecting the difference into an identity prompt gives outputs dominated by echo/mapping examples ("cat -> cat", "1135 -> 1135", "This -> This"), short instructional fragments and simple code snippets ("```python", "def is_prime..."), and a didactic tone ("This is a good start. You've successfully echoed the input."). That strongly supports the view that the difference makes the model more likely to open with example/echo/instructional continuations.

Uncertainty / caveats
- The two tendencies (example/echo/instructional style vs. vivid/headline/promotional single-word starts) may be two facets of the same shift (e.g., a push toward "exemplifying" or "attention-getting" openings), or they may be distinct effects mixed in the difference vector. The evidence does not let me confidently name a single, specific training objective (e.g., "contrastive example demonstration fine-tuning") — only that the first-token bias changed in interpretable ways described above.
